newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks seen up, Greenspan impact lingers.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks seen up, Greenspan impact lingers.

text.p: Argentine stocks were seen rising at the opening Thursday, traders said, as investors continued to see value in the market.
"The market is set to open with a moderate rise. The statements by (U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman) Alan Greenspan were key for investors," said Miguel Daneri, a trader at Boston Securities.
Earlier in the week Greenspan painted an upbeat picture of the U.S. economy, in his half-yearly Humphry-Hawkins testimony to Congress, dispelling worries of a U.S. rate hike.
"The market continues to be positive. The banking segment presents an attractive investment," said a stock analyst.
On Wednesday the blue-chip MerVal index .MERV rose 1.01 percent to 821.70, building on Tuesday's 2.9 percent jump, which snapped a sharp losing spell.
Traders said the market is likely to be further supported by the quarterly earnings season which kicks off at the beginning of August.
Company results are likely to be strong as they increasingly benefit from Argentina's high growth, analysts said.
